display.title: Aharon and the Golden Calf: Seeing the Good in Every Jew
display.summary_short: From Parshas Ki Sisa: Moshe Rabbeinu gives Aharon a way to explain the golden calf, and a cheder teacher finds a stolen watch with his own eyes closed.
display.summary_long: The storyteller explains that the most important message of every parsha is Ahavas Yisroel. In this week's parsha the Yidden make the golden calf, and Aharon seems to help them, though he was really trying to delay them. When Moshe Rabbeinu comes down, he does not shout at Aharon. Instead he asks, 'What did this people do to you?', giving Aharon a way to explain himself and showing that this was not the real Aharon. A mashal follows: a rebbe whose pupil kicks a friend assumes something must have upset the boy, because he is really good. Then a story from Eretz Yisroel: when a valuable watch disappears in cheder, an elderly Chassid who teaches there has all the boys close their eyes and searches their pockets. Years later a grown man thanks him for never shaming him, and learns that the teacher had kept his own eyes closed too. Finally, Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka once turned her face away when a bachur bumped into her, so that she would never know who it was.
display.lesson: When a Jew does something wrong, judge him favorably, do not shame him, and show him that you know he is really good; this Ahavas Yisroel will bring Moshiach.

characters: an elderly Chassid, a cheder teacher in Eretz Yisroel
the boy who took the watch
